GASTRIC.clue: Ulcer worsened by food; biopsy it because carcinoma can look the same
GASTRIC.rationale: Gastric ulcers often hurt with eating. Unlike duodenal ulcers, they must be biopsied to exclude malignancy; NSAIDs and H. pylori are the usual benign causes.

PULMONIC.clue: Right-sided semilunar valve; congenital narrowing causes a systolic murmur at the upper left sternal border
PULMONIC.rationale: Pulmonic stenosis is usually congenital. The murmur is a crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur, and wide splitting of the second heart sound may occur.

IMPETIGO.clue: Honey-crusted lesions from staph or strep; kidney inflammation can follow, rheumatic fever does not
IMPETIGO.rationale: Impetigo is a honey-crusted superficial infection from Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. Limited disease is treated with topical mupirocin; poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis can follow skin infection; rheumatic fever follows pharyngitis, not impetigo.

DIABETES.clue: Hyperglycemia disease diagnosed by fasting glucose, a two-hour challenge, a symptomatic random glucose, or A1C
DIABETES.rationale: Diabetes is diagnosed by fasting glucose at least 126, a 2-hour glucose at least 200, a random glucose at least 200 with symptoms, or A1C at least 6.5 percent, confirmed unless the presentation is unequivocal. Metformin is first-line when kidney function allows, with additional agents chosen for heart, kidney, and weight outcomes.

DUODENAL.clue: Ulcer that typically hurts when the stomach is empty and is strongly linked to H. pylori
DUODENAL.rationale: Duodenal ulcers usually cause pain that improves with food and returns when the stomach empties. Helicobacter pylori and NSAIDs are the main causes; perforation produces sudden pain and free air.

FERRITIN.clue: Storage marker that is very low in iron deficiency and very high, with a high transferrin saturation, in hereditary iron overload
FERRITIN.rationale: Ferritin reflects iron stores and is also an acute-phase reactant, so a normal value does not fully exclude iron deficiency during inflammation. A very high ferritin with high transferrin saturation suggests hemochromatosis.

SYPHILIS.clue: Painless chancre, then a rash that includes palms and soles; penicillin is the only reliable cure
SYPHILIS.rationale: Syphilis begins with a painless chancre, then a disseminated rash often involving palms and soles, and can end in gummas, aortitis, or neurosyphilis. Nontreponemal tests screen and titers follow treatment; a treponemal test confirms; penicillin is required, with desensitization if the patient is allergic, especially in pregnancy.

HEBERDEN.clue: Bony nodes of the distal finger joints in osteoarthritis
HEBERDEN.rationale: Heberden nodes are bony enlargement of the DIP joints in osteoarthritis. They are not inflammatory synovitis; osteoarthritis worsens with use, spares the MCP joints, and shows joint-space narrowing and osteophytes.

EPIDURAL.clue: Lens-shaped arterial bleed, often after a temporal blow with a lucid interval
EPIDURAL.rationale: Epidural hematoma is usually arterial, from the middle meningeal artery, and is lens-shaped because sutures limit it. A lucid interval after head trauma is classic; it is a neurosurgical emergency.

CHADWICK.clue: Bluish cervix and vagina that is an early sign of pregnancy
CHADWICK.rationale: Chadwick sign is venous congestion that turns the cervix and vaginal mucosa bluish in early pregnancy. It is a presumptive sign, not proof of an intrauterine pregnancy.

GLAUCOMA.clue: Acute angle closure has a mid-dilated pupil and a rock-hard eye; the open-angle form is silent
GLAUCOMA.rationale: Acute angle-closure glaucoma is an emergency: a painful red eye, halos, a mid-dilated pupil, nausea, and a rock-hard globe. Pressure is lowered medically and then with a laser iridotomy; open-angle glaucoma is silent cupping found on screening.

DYSTONIA.clue: Sustained muscle contraction from an antipsychotic; treat with benztropine or diphenhydramine
DYSTONIA.rationale: Acute dystonia is a sustained contraction, such as torticollis or an oculogyric crisis, hours to days after a dopamine blocker. Intramuscular benztropine or diphenhydramine reverses it; young men on high-potency typical antipsychotics are at highest risk.

RIFAMPIN.clue: Tuberculosis drug that turns body fluids orange and induces many liver enzymes
RIFAMPIN.rationale: Rifampin is a key tuberculosis drug and is also used for some meningococcal and Haemophilus contacts. It stains fluids orange, is hepatotoxic, and is a potent CYP inducer that lowers levels of many drugs, including warfarin and oral contraceptives.

PRERENAL.clue: Kidney injury from poor perfusion; sodium retention is avid and the sediment is bland
PRERENAL.rationale: Prerenal azotemia is inadequate renal perfusion with intact tubules, so the urine is concentrated and sodium-poor. The fraction of excreted sodium is typically below 1 percent; restoring volume reverses it if ischemia has not yet injured tubules.

ETHYLENE.clue: Antifreeze alcohol that causes an anion-gap acidosis, oxalate crystals, and kidney failure
ETHYLENE.rationale: Ethylene glycol causes intoxication, then an anion-gap acidosis, hypocalcemia, calcium-oxalate crystals, and acute kidney injury. Fluorescence of the urine is unreliable; fomepizole and, when severe, hemodialysis are the treatment.

STENOSIS.clue: Fixed valve narrowing; the aortic form radiates to the carotids and limits cardiac output when severe
STENOSIS.rationale: Valve stenosis obstructs forward flow. Aortic stenosis radiates to the carotids; mitral stenosis causes a diastolic rumble after an opening snap.

FURUNCLE.clue: A boil: a staphylococcal abscess centered on a hair follicle
FURUNCLE.rationale: A furuncle is a staphylococcal abscess of a hair follicle. Warm compresses may drain a small one; larger ones are incised; recurrent boils prompt a search for colonization and for diabetes.

ACARBOSE.clue: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor whose hypoglycemia must be treated with glucose, not table sugar
ACARBOSE.rationale: Acarbose delays carbohydrate absorption and causes gas and diarrhea. If hypoglycemia occurs, give glucose itself; sucrose and complex sugars will not be absorbed quickly enough to help.

LEADPIPE.clue: Loss of colonic haustra on a contrast study in chronic ulcerative colitis
LEADPIPE.rationale: The lead-pipe colon is a featureless, shortened colon from chronic ulcerative colitis with loss of haustral folds. It is a radiographic description, not an acute finding.

CODOCYTE.clue: Target-shaped red cell of thalassemia, hemoglobinopathy, liver disease, and asplenia
CODOCYTE.rationale: Codocytes, or target cells, have a central hemoglobin bump. They are seen in thalassemia, hemoglobin C and sickle disease, obstructive liver disease, and after splenectomy.

BOTULISM.clue: Descending flaccid paralysis and double vision after home-canned food, or after honey in an infant
BOTULISM.rationale: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release and causes descending paralysis, diplopia, and a dry mouth, without fever. Sources include home-canned food, honey in infants, and contaminated wounds; antitoxin is given; antibiotics are not used for infant botulism.

BOUCHARD.clue: Bony nodes of the proximal finger joints in osteoarthritis
BOUCHARD.rationale: Bouchard nodes are bony swelling of the PIP joints in osteoarthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis also involves the PIP joints but is inflammatory, symmetric, and spares the DIP joints while involving the MCPs.

SUBDURAL.clue: Crescent-shaped venous bleed in an older adult or a person with brain atrophy
SUBDURAL.rationale: Subdural hematoma is bleeding from bridging veins and spreads in a crescent along the hemisphere. Older adults and people with alcohol use disorder are at risk because atrophy stretches those veins; symptoms can fluctuate.

MASTITIS.clue: Breast infection during nursing, usually staph; keep emptying the breast and give an antistaphylococcal antibiotic
MASTITIS.rationale: Lactational mastitis is a painful wedge of erythema, usually Staphylococcus aureus, and sometimes MRSA. The parent continues breastfeeding or pumping; dicloxacillin or cephalexin is typical, with MRSA coverage if risk is high; a fluctuant abscess is drained.

FLOATERS.clue: New specks plus flashes and a curtain over vision mean the retina may be detaching
FLOATERS.rationale: Sudden floaters and flashes, especially with a curtain of vision loss, suggest retinal tear or detachment and need same-day ophthalmology. A slowly increasing single floater in an older adult is often a benign vitreous change, but new showers are not.

PRIAPISM.clue: Prolonged painful erection; a classic adverse effect of trazodone and a complication of sickle cell disease
PRIAPISM.rationale: Priapism is an erection lasting more than about four hours and is a urologic emergency. Trazodone and other alpha blockers, sickle cell disease, and intracavernosal injections are classic causes; ischemic priapism is aspirated and injected with a sympathomimetic.

ASBESTOS.clue: Fiber exposure causing pleural plaques and mesothelioma; it multiplies smoking-related lung cancer risk
ASBESTOS.rationale: Asbestos causes pleural plaques, interstitial fibrosis that is often basilar, mesothelioma, and lung cancer. Smoking multiplies the lung-cancer risk but is not required for mesothelioma; latency is measured in decades.

STRUVITE.clue: Staghorn stone from a urease-positive organism such as Proteus; the urine is alkaline
STRUVITE.rationale: Struvite stones form when urease-producing bacteria, such as Proteus, alkalinize the urine and precipitate magnesium ammonium phosphate. They can fill the pelvis as a staghorn calculus and must be removed, not just treated with antibiotics.

METHANOL.clue: Wood alcohol that causes visual loss and injury to the putamen; block its metabolism
METHANOL.rationale: Methanol causes an anion-gap acidosis and visual snow or blindness from formic acid, with putaminal injury. Fomepizole blocks formation of the toxic metabolite; folate is often given because it helps clear formate.

FRICTION.clue: Scratchy three-component rub heard when the inflamed pericardial surfaces rub
FRICTION.rationale: A pericardial friction rub is scratchy and may have systolic and diastolic components. It supports pericarditis along with pain that eases leaning forward and diffuse ST elevation.

MELANOMA.clue: Pigmented malignancy judged by asymmetry, border, color, diameter, and change; thickness drives prognosis
MELANOMA.rationale: Melanoma is assessed with the ABCDE rule, and Breslow thickness is the key prognostic measure. Any changing or ugly-duckling lesion is excised, not frozen or watched indefinitely; sun and tanning beds are the modifiable risks.

INCRETIN.clue: Gut-hormone pathway mimicked by drugs that raise insulin, slow the stomach, and reduce weight
INCRETIN.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonists increase glucose-dependent insulin release, slow gastric emptying, and cause weight loss, with benefit in atherosclerotic disease. Nausea is common; they are avoided with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2.

PANCREAS.clue: Epigastric pain boring to the back with a high lipase; gallstones and alcohol are the leading causes
PANCREAS.rationale: Acute pancreatitis is epigastric pain radiating to the back with lipase at least three times normal. Gallstones and alcohol are the most common causes; early fluid resuscitation is the priority; antibiotics are for infected necrosis, not routine use.

TEARDROP.clue: Red-cell shape on the smear of primary myelofibrosis
TEARDROP.rationale: Dacrocytes, or teardrop cells, are classic for primary myelofibrosis, in which marrow is replaced by fibrosis and the spleen becomes the site of blood production. A dry tap and a huge spleen support the diagnosis.

SHINGLES.clue: Painful vesicles in one dermatome; a lesion on the nasal tip threatens the eye
SHINGLES.rationale: Herpes zoster is reactivation of varicella in a single dermatome, with pain that may precede the rash. Hutchinson sign, a vesicle on the nasal tip, means nasociliary involvement and risk to the eye; antiviral therapy is most useful when started early.

REACTIVE.clue: Arthritis, eye inflammation, and urethritis after chlamydia or a bacterial diarrheal illness
REACTIVE.rationale: Reactive arthritis follows Chlamydia or invasive bacterial gastroenteritis and classically combines arthritis, uveitis or conjunctivitis, and urethritis. HLA-B27 is often present; treat the triggering infection if it is still present, and use NSAIDs for the joints.

MIGRAINE.clue: Pulsatile unilateral headache with nausea and light sensitivity; aura means avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives
MIGRAINE.rationale: Migraine is a recurrent pulsatile headache with nausea or photo- and phonophobia, with or without aura. Treat early with an NSAID or a triptan; aura is a reason to avoid combined hormonal contraceptives because of stroke risk.

ASHERMAN.clue: Uterine synechiae after curettage causing amenorrhea
ASHERMAN.rationale: Asherman syndrome is intrauterine adhesions, usually after curettage, causing amenorrhea, infertility, and cyclic pain if endometrium is trapped. Hysteroscopy both diagnoses and treats it.

DELUSION.clue: Fixed false belief held despite evidence, a positive symptom of a primary psychotic disorder
DELUSION.rationale: A delusion is a fixed false belief not shared by the person's culture. With hallucinations and disorganized speech it defines psychosis; duration and mood symptoms separate schizophrenia, schizophreniform disorder, and schizoaffective disorder.

PANCOAST.clue: Apical lung tumor causing shoulder pain, hand weakness, and a small pupil with a drooping lid
PANCOAST.rationale: A Pancoast tumor at the lung apex invades the brachial plexus and cervical sympathetic chain. Shoulder or arm pain, intrinsic hand wasting, and Horner syndrome are the classic cluster; non-small cell lung cancer is the usual histology.

PROSTATE.clue: Gland whose cancer presents with a hard nodule and osteoblastic spine metastases
PROSTATE.rationale: Prostate cancer is a disease of older men. A hard nodule on rectal exam or a rising PSA prompts biopsy discussion; metastases are osteoblastic and cause high alkaline phosphatase and back pain; screening is a shared decision.

TRICUSPID.clue: Right-sided atrioventricular valve; its regurgitant murmur grows louder on inspiration
TRICUSPID.rationale: Tricuspid regurgitation is often functional from pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular dilation. Inspiration increases venous return and makes right-sided murmurs louder.

PSORIASIS.clue: Well-demarcated salmon plaques with silvery scale on the extensor surfaces
PSORIASIS.rationale: Psoriasis is well-demarcated salmon plaques with silvery scale on extensor surfaces. Pinpoint bleeding under a lifted scale, new lesions at sites of trauma, nail pitting, and arthritis are classic companions.

SINUSITIS.clue: Most facial pain with a cold is viral; use an antibiotic if symptoms are severe, double-worsening, or last past ten days
SINUSITIS.rationale: Acute rhinosinusitis is usually viral. Antibiotics, typically amoxicillin-clavulanate, are reserved for symptoms lasting beyond 10 days, severe symptoms, or double worsening; chronic disease looks for allergy, anatomy, and, in selected patients, immunodeficiency.

METFORMIN.clue: First-line biguanide that lowers hepatic glucose output and does not cause hypoglycemia by itself
METFORMIN.rationale: Metformin decreases hepatic gluconeogenesis. It does not cause hypoglycemia when used alone and often causes diarrhea; it is avoided when eGFR is below 30 because of lactic acidosis risk, and it is held around iodinated contrast when kidney function is reduced or unstable.

ESOPHAGUS.clue: Tube whose distal adenocarcinoma follows Barrett metaplasia and whose proximal squamous cancer follows smoking and alcohol
ESOPHAGUS.rationale: Esophageal adenocarcinoma arises distally from Barrett esophagus. Squamous cell carcinoma arises more proximally and is linked to smoking and alcohol; progressive dysphagia, solids then liquids, is the classic symptom.

COBALAMIN.clue: Deficiency causing megaloblastic anemia plus dorsal-column and corticospinal neuropathy
COBALAMIN.rationale: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and subacute combined degeneration of the cord. Both homocysteine and methylmalonic acid are high; causes include pernicious anemia, terminal-ileum disease, vegan diet, and metformin.

ACYCLOVIR.clue: Nucleoside analog for herpes simplex and zoster; keep the patient hydrated to protect the kidney
ACYCLOVIR.rationale: Acyclovir treats HSV and varicella-zoster. Intravenous doses can crystallize in the kidney if the patient is not hydrated; empiric intravenous therapy is started for suspected herpes encephalitis before PCR returns.

PSORIATIC.clue: Sausage digits and pencil-in-cup joints with nail pitting; the rash may hide in the scalp or the gluteal cleft
PSORIATIC.rationale: Psoriatic arthritis can involve the DIP joints, cause dactylitis and nail pitting, and show pencil-in-cup erosions. The skin disease may be modest or hidden; NSAIDs, methotrexate, and TNF or IL-17 inhibitors are used.

AMAUROSIS.clue: Curtain-like monocular vision loss that resolves, a vascular warning from the carotid or from giant-cell arteritis
AMAUROSIS.rationale: Amaurosis fugax is a transient monocular curtain of vision loss from ipsilateral carotid embolism or, in an older adult with headache, from giant cell arteritis. It is a stroke-equivalent and needs urgent evaluation.

ABRUPTION.clue: Painful third-trimester bleeding with a firm, tender uterus; clotting factors can be consumed
ABRUPTION.rationale: Placental abruption is premature separation causing painful bleeding, a hypertonic uterus, and fetal distress. Hemorrhage may be concealed; hypertension, trauma, and cocaine are risks; DIC is the coagulation complication.

BUPROPION.clue: Antidepressant that helps smoking cessation and spares sexual function; avoid it in seizure and eating disorders
BUPROPION.rationale: Bupropion inhibits norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake. It does not cause sexual dysfunction and aids smoking cessation; it lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in bulimia, anorexia, and seizure disorders.

EMPHYSEMA.clue: Alveolar destruction with a low diffusing capacity; smoking favors the upper lobes
EMPHYSEMA.rationale: Emphysema destroys alveolar walls and reduces elastic recoil and DLCO. Smoking-related disease is centrilobular and upper-lobe; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is panacinar and basilar.

POSTRENAL.clue: Kidney injury from obstruction; ultrasound looks for hydronephrosis
POSTRENAL.rationale: Postrenal injury requires obstruction of both kidneys or of a solitary kidney, or urethral obstruction. Ultrasound shows hydronephrosis unless the obstruction is extremely early or the patient is profoundly volume depleted; relieve the blockage.

METHYLENE.clue: Blue dye that treats methemoglobinemia from benzocaine or dapsone; avoid it in G6PD deficiency
METHYLENE.rationale: Methylene blue reduces methemoglobin via an NADPH-dependent pathway. It is the antidote for symptomatic methemoglobinemia from local anesthetics or dapsone; it does not work, and can hemolyze, in G6PD deficiency.

TAMPONADE.clue: Pericardial fluid under pressure that equalizes diastolic filling and drops cardiac output
TAMPONADE.rationale: Tamponade causes hypotension, jugular venous distention, and an exaggerated inspiratory drop in systolic pressure. Echocardiography shows chamber collapse, and drainage is the treatment.

FASCIITIS.clue: Rapidly spreading deep soft-tissue infection with pain out of proportion; this is a surgical emergency
FASCIITIS.rationale: Necrotizing fasciitis causes pain out of proportion, systemic toxicity, and rapid spread along fascia, sometimes with crepitus. Group A strep and polymicrobial infection are typical; immediate surgical debridement plus broad antibiotics, including clindamycin for toxin suppression, are required.

GLYBURIDE.clue: Sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin release and can cause hypoglycemia; avoid it when kidney function is poor
GLYBURIDE.rationale: Glyburide closes potassium channels on beta cells and forces insulin release, so hypoglycemia is the main risk. Active metabolites accumulate in kidney disease, so it is a poor choice in older adults and in CKD.

ACHALASIA.clue: Bird-beak esophagus with failure of the lower sphincter to relax; Chagas disease can mimic it
ACHALASIA.rationale: Achalasia is loss of inhibitory neurons in the esophageal myenteric plexus, so the lower sphincter fails to relax and peristalsis is absent. Dysphagia is to solids and liquids; trypanosoma cruzi can produce the same picture.

LEUKEMOID.clue: Reactive extreme leukocytosis with a high leukocyte alkaline phosphatase, unlike chronic myeloid leukemia
LEUKEMOID.rationale: A leukemoid reaction is a benign extreme neutrophilia from infection or inflammation. Toxic granulation and a high leukocyte alkaline phosphatase separate it from CML, in which the alkaline phosphatase is low.

RHEUMATIC.clue: Immune disease after strep throat, with carditis and migratory arthritis; it does not follow skin infection
RHEUMATIC.rationale: Acute rheumatic fever follows group A streptococcal pharyngitis, not impetigo. Carditis, especially mitral valvulitis, is the morbidity; treatment is antibiotics plus anti-inflammatory therapy, then long-term penicillin prophylaxis.

NURSEMAID.clue: Radial-head subluxation in a toddler pulled by the arm; reduce it by supinating and flexing
NURSEMAID.rationale: Nursemaid's elbow is radial-head subluxation from longitudinal traction on a pronated toddler arm. The child will not use the arm; supination and flexion, or hyperpronation, reduces it; films are normal.

LHERMITTE.clue: Electric sensation down the spine when the neck is flexed, a sign of cervical cord demyelination
LHERMITTE.rationale: Lhermitte sign is an electric shock down the spine with neck flexion. It indicates a cervical spinal cord lesion, classically multiple sclerosis, but it is not specific.

ECLAMPSIA.clue: New seizure in pregnancy hypertension; magnesium is the anticonvulsant and delivery is definitive
ECLAMPSIA.rationale: Eclampsia is a seizure in a patient with preeclampsia, not explained by another neurologic disease. Magnesium sulfate treats and prevents the seizure; delivery is the definitive treatment of the underlying disease.

AKATHISIA.clue: Inner restlessness from antipsychotics; a beta blocker can help
AKATHISIA.rationale: Akathisia is a subjective urge to move and is an extrapyramidal effect of antipsychotics and some antiemetics. Lowering the dose, a beta blocker, or a benzodiazepine is used; it is a risk factor for agitation and self-harm.

PERTUSSIS.clue: Whooping cough with post-tussive emesis; treat the patient and close contacts with a macrolide
PERTUSSIS.rationale: Pertussis has a catarrhal phase then paroxysmal cough with a whoop and post-tussive vomiting, plus marked lymphocytosis. A macrolide is given to the patient and close contacts; the cough can persist after the organism is cleared.

NEPHROTIC.clue: Proteinuria above 3.5 grams a day with edema, low albumin, and high lipids
NEPHROTIC.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome is heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia. Urine may show oval fat bodies; thrombosis risk is high; causes include minimal change, FSGS, membranous nephropathy, diabetes, and amyloid.

ALTERNANS.clue: Beat-to-beat change in QRS amplitude, a clue to a large pericardial effusion with tamponade
ALTERNANS.rationale: Electrical alternans is beat-to-beat variation in QRS amplitude from the heart swinging in a large pericardial effusion. It supports tamponade when the clinical picture fits.

PEMPHIGUS.clue: Flaccid blisters and oral erosions from antibodies to the protein that holds keratinocytes together
PEMPHIGUS.rationale: Pemphigus vulgaris is IgG against desmoglein, so keratinocytes separate and blisters are flaccid, with oral erosions often first. Nikolsky sign is positive; immunofluorescence shows a net-like IgG pattern; steroids and rituximab are used.

HASHIMOTO.clue: Most common hypothyroidism where iodine is sufficient; antiperoxidase antibodies and a firm goiter
HASHIMOTO.rationale: Hashimoto thyroiditis is autoimmune thyroid destruction with antiperoxidase antibodies, causing hypothyroidism and a firm goiter. Severe decompensation with hypothermia is treated with intravenous thyroid hormone plus steroids until adrenal failure is excluded.

CORKSCREW.clue: Barium pattern of diffuse esophageal spasm
CORKSCREW.rationale: Diffuse esophageal spasm produces a corkscrew esophagus on barium swallow and chest pain with intermittent dysphagia. Calcium-channel blockers or nitrates are used for symptoms.

AMIODARONE.clue: Class III antiarrhythmic that can injure lung, thyroid, and liver and deposits in the cornea and skin
AMIODARONE.rationale: Amiodarone is used for atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. Before and during therapy, monitor pulmonary, thyroid, and liver function because of pulmonary toxicity, hypo- or hyperthyroidism, and hepatitis.

MULTIFORME.clue: Target lesions, often after herpes simplex; this is distinct from widespread drug-related skin necrosis
MULTIFORME.rationale: Erythema multiforme is target lesions, often acral, usually triggered by herpes simplex and sometimes by Mycoplasma. Mucosal involvement can occur; it is separated from Stevens-Johnson syndrome, which is a more severe drug reaction.

EUGLYCEMIC.clue: Ketoacidosis with a near-normal glucose, a risk of sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitor drugs
EUGLYCEMIC.rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause diabetic ketoacidosis with glucose that is not very high. Stop the drug during illness and before surgery, and do not be reassured by a near-normal glucose if the patient is acidotic.

OCTREOTIDE.clue: Somatostatin analog used for variceal bleeding and for acromegaly or a carcinoid syndrome
OCTREOTIDE.rationale: Octreotide reduces splanchnic blood flow and is given in acute variceal hemorrhage. It also treats acromegaly and the secretory symptoms of carcinoid syndrome.

PERNICIOUS.clue: Autoimmune loss of intrinsic factor leading to vitamin B12 deficiency
PERNICIOUS.rationale: Pernicious anemia is autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells with intrinsic-factor antibodies, causing B12 deficiency. There is an increased risk of gastric carcinoma; parenteral or high-dose oral B12 replaces the vitamin.

DIPHTHERIA.clue: Pharyngeal gray pseudomembrane and a bull neck; give antitoxin plus an antibiotic
DIPHTHERIA.rationale: Corynebacterium diphtheriae produces a toxin and an adherent gray pharyngeal membrane that bleeds when peeled, with a bull neck. Airway obstruction and myocarditis kill; antitoxin is given as soon as the disease is suspected, plus an antibiotic.

RHEUMATOID.clue: Symmetric synovitis of the small joints of the hands that spares the furthest knuckles; methotrexate is the anchor drug
RHEUMATOID.rationale: Rheumatoid arthritis is symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis of the MCP and PIP joints with prolonged morning stiffness, sparing the DIPs. Anti-CCP antibody is specific; methotrexate is the anchor disease-modifying drug unless contraindicated.

CONCUSSION.clue: Mild traumatic brain injury with transient neurologic change; image only when red flags are present
CONCUSSION.rationale: Concussion is a functional brain injury with headache, confusion, or amnesia, usually without a lesion on CT. Red flags such as worsening consciousness, repeated vomiting, or focal signs prompt imaging; return to activity is graded.

CARBOPROST.clue: Prostaglandin for postpartum hemorrhage that is contraindicated in asthma
CARBOPROST.rationale: Carboprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analog used for uterine atony after oxytocin. It can cause bronchospasm and is contraindicated in asthma; diarrhea and fever are common.

ADENOVIRUS.clue: Virus of watery pink eye with a node in front of the ear
ADENOVIRUS.rationale: Adenovirus causes highly contagious conjunctivitis with watery discharge and a preauricular node, and pharyngoconjunctival fever. It is supportive care; bacterial conjunctivitis is purulent; allergic conjunctivitis itches.

DEPRESSION.clue: Low mood or anhedonia for two weeks with sleep, energy, or concentration change; an SSRI is first-line
DEPRESSION.rationale: Major depression requires at least two weeks of depressed mood or anhedonia plus additional symptoms that impair function. SSRIs are first-line medication; screen for bipolar history so antidepressant monotherapy is not started in unrecognized mania.

BRONCHITIS.clue: Productive cough for three months in two consecutive years, the blue-bloater pattern
BRONCHITIS.rationale: Chronic bronchitis is a clinical diagnosis: productive cough at least three months a year for two years, without another cause. Patients are often hypoxemic and hypercapnic.

MEMBRANOUS.clue: Nephrotic syndrome of adults linked to solid tumors, hepatitis B, and a phospholipase-receptor antibody
MEMBRANOUS.rationale: Membranous nephropathy presents as nephrotic syndrome. It is associated with solid tumors, hepatitis B, lupus, and PLA2R antibodies in the primary form; renal-vein thrombosis is a particular risk.

SALICYLATE.clue: Overdose causing ringing in the ears and a respiratory alkalosis mixed with an anion-gap acidosis
SALICYLATE.rationale: Salicylate overdose causes tinnitus, fever, and an early respiratory alkalosis plus an anion-gap metabolic acidosis. Alkalinization with bicarbonate traps the drug, and hemodialysis is used for severe levels, kidney failure, or altered mentation.

FLECAINIDE.clue: Class Ic antiarrhythmic for atrial fibrillation in a structurally normal heart; avoid it after infarction
FLECAINIDE.rationale: Flecainide is a potent sodium-channel blocker used for atrial fibrillation in patients without structural heart disease or coronary disease. The CAST trial showed harm when this drug class was used after myocardial infarction.

MARGINATUM.clue: Evanescent serpiginous rash that is a major finding of acute rheumatic fever
MARGINATUM.rationale: Erythema marginatum is a fleeting, serpiginous, nonpruritic rash of acute rheumatic fever and is one of the major Jones criteria. It is easy to miss because it comes and goes.

POSTPARTUM.clue: Painless thyroid inflammation after delivery that can swing from high to low hormone
POSTPARTUM.rationale: Postpartum thyroiditis is a painless autoimmune inflammation with low radioiodine uptake, a hyperthyroid phase, then hypothyroidism. Many recover, but some remain permanently hypothyroid and need levothyroxine.

GASTRINOMA.clue: Gastrin-secreting tumor causing refractory ulcers and diarrhea; screen for MEN1
GASTRINOMA.rationale: A gastrinoma causes Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: multiple or refractory peptic ulcers and diarrhea from acid inactivation of enzymes. Measure fasting gastrin, and evaluate for MEN1.

SPHEROCYTE.clue: Round red cell of hereditary membrane defects and of immune hemolysis
SPHEROCYTE.rationale: Spherocytes are seen in hereditary spherocytosis and in immune hemolysis. Hereditary spherocytosis has a high MCHC, a positive osmotic-fragility test, pigment gallstones, and an aplastic crisis from parvovirus; splenectomy after vaccines is definitive for severe disease.

PARVOVIRUS.clue: Virus of slapped-cheek rash in children and of aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease
PARVOVIRUS.rationale: Parvovirus B19 causes fifth disease, a slapped-cheek rash, and can cause an aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease or other hemolytic anemias because it infects red-cell precursors. In pregnancy it can cause hydrops.

ANKYLOSING.clue: Young man with sacroiliitis and morning back stiffness that improves with activity; the spine can look like bamboo
ANKYLOSING.rationale: Ankylosing spondylitis is an HLA-B27-associated inflammatory back disease of young men, with sacroiliitis, reduced chest expansion, and a bamboo spine. Pain improves with activity; an NSAID is first-line; uveitis and aortitis are extra-articular features.

TRIGEMINAL.clue: Cranial nerve whose neuralgia causes electric facial pain; carbamazepine is first-line
TRIGEMINAL.rationale: Trigeminal neuralgia is lancinating pain in a trigeminal distribution, triggered by light touch. Carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine is first-line; in a young patient, think of multiple sclerosis.

AGALACTIAE.clue: Group B organism screened by rectovaginal culture late in pregnancy and treated during labor
AGALACTIAE.rationale: Streptococcus agalactiae is group B streptococcus. Rectovaginal culture is done at about 36 to 37 weeks, and intrapartum penicillin is given to carriers to prevent early-onset neonatal sepsis; a penicillin-allergic patient at high anaphylaxis risk receives a susceptibility-guided alternative.

SERTRALINE.clue: SSRI often chosen when depression coexists with heart disease; it still needs weeks to work
SERTRALINE.rationale: Sertraline has fewer CYP interactions than some other SSRIs and is commonly chosen in patients with cardiac disease and in breastfeeding. Like other SSRIs it has a delayed onset and can cause sexual dysfunction and hyponatremia.

THUMBPRINT.clue: Lateral neck-film sign of epiglottitis in a drooling, tripoding patient
THUMBPRINT.rationale: The thumbprint sign is a swollen epiglottis on a lateral neck radiograph. Do not agitate the patient or examine the throat; secure the airway in a controlled setting and give an antibiotic that covers Haemophilus influenzae.

MYOCARDITIS.clue: Inflammation of heart muscle, often viral, with chest pain, troponin rise, and reduced function
MYOCARDITIS.rationale: Myocarditis often follows a viral illness such as coxsackievirus, with chest pain, elevated troponin, and reduced pump function. It can mimic infarction and can present as a new cardiomyopathy.

INFECTIOSUM.clue: Slapped-cheek illness of school-age children caused by parvovirus
INFECTIOSUM.rationale: Erythema infectiosum, fifth disease, is parvovirus B19: a slapped cheek then a lacy trunk rash. The child is usually no longer infectious once the rash appears; the danger is to the fetus and to patients with hemolytic anemia.

KIESSELBACH.clue: Anterior septal vascular plexus that is the usual source of a nosebleed
KIESSELBACH.rationale: Kiesselbach plexus is the anastomotic area on the anterior nasal septum and the source of most epistaxis. Local trauma, dry air, and nose picking are the usual precipitants.

PARATHYROID.clue: Gland whose adenoma raises calcium and lowers phosphate, causing stones, bone pain, and constipation
PARATHYROID.rationale: Primary hyperparathyroidism, usually a single adenoma, causes high calcium, low phosphate, and a high or inappropriately normal PTH. Stones, bone pain, constipation, and psychiatric symptoms are the classic effects; surgery is definitive for those who meet criteria.

COBBLESTONE.clue: Mucosal pattern of deep linear ulcers separated by swollen islands in Crohn disease
COBBLESTONE.rationale: Cobblestoning is the endoscopic look of intersecting linear ulcers in Crohn disease. It reflects transmural, discontinuous inflammation rather than the continuous mucosal disease of ulcerative colitis.

THALASSEMIA.clue: Microcytic anemia with normal iron stores; the major form shows a crew-cut skull
THALASSEMIA.rationale: Thalassemia is impaired globin-chain synthesis. The trait is microcytic with a normal or high red-cell count and normal iron studies, unlike iron deficiency; beta major causes severe anemia, chipmunk facies, and a crew-cut skull from marrow expansion.

PHARYNGITIS.clue: Sore throat; test and treat group A strep to prevent rheumatic fever, not to prevent glomerulonephritis
PHARYNGITIS.rationale: Most pharyngitis is viral. The Centor criteria guide testing for group A strep; treating strep pharyngitis prevents rheumatic fever but does not reliably prevent poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

SCLERODERMA.clue: Skin-thickening disease; the diffuse form risks lung fibrosis and a renal crisis treated with an ACE inhibitor
SCLERODERMA.rationale: Systemic sclerosis thickens skin. Diffuse disease is associated with anti-Scl-70 and with interstitial lung disease and scleroderma renal crisis, which is treated with an ACE inhibitor; limited disease has anticentromere antibody and the CREST features.

PSEUDOTUMOR.clue: Obese young woman with headache and papilledema but normal imaging; opening pressure is high
PSEUDOTUMOR.rationale: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension causes headache and papilledema with normal imaging and an elevated opening pressure. It affects young women with obesity and is linked to vitamin A and tetracyclines; acetazolamide and weight loss are first-line; vision is the endpoint.

TROPHOBLAST.clue: Gestational tissue that, when malignant, spreads to the lungs and is followed with the pregnancy hormone
TROPHOBLAST.rationale: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, including choriocarcinoma, follows a mole, abortion, or pregnancy and spreads hematogenously, often to the lung. hCG is the marker. These tumors are highly sensitive to chemotherapy.

NEOVASCULAR.clue: Fragile new retinal vessels of proliferative diabetic eye disease that bleed and scar
NEOVASCULAR.rationale: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy grows neovascular vessels that bleed into the vitreous and cause traction detachment. Tight glucose and blood-pressure control prevent it; laser or anti-VEGF injections treat high-risk disease; an annual dilated exam is the screen.

HALOPERIDOL.clue: High-potency typical antipsychotic with a high risk of extrapyramidal effects and QT prolongation
HALOPERIDOL.rationale: Haloperidol strongly blocks D2 receptors, so extrapyramidal symptoms are common and anticholinergic effects are fewer than with low-potency agents. It prolongs QT; all antipsychotics carry a mortality warning in dementia-related psychosis.

ANTITRYPSIN.clue: Protein deficiency causing early basilar emphysema and liver disease
ANTITRYPSIN.rationale: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes panacinar emphysema, classically basal, in younger adults, including nonsmokers, plus liver disease from retained protein. A low serum level and genotyping confirm it.

GOODPASTURE.clue: Lung hemorrhage plus glomerulonephritis with linear basement-membrane antibody; plasmapheresis is required
GOODPASTURE.rationale: Goodpasture syndrome is anti-GBM antibody disease attacking lung and kidney, with linear IgG on biopsy. Young men who smoke are classic; treatment is plasmapheresis plus cyclophosphamide and steroids.

ISOPROPANOL.clue: Rubbing alcohol that causes ketosis without an anion-gap acidosis
ISOPROPANOL.rationale: Isopropanol is metabolized to acetone, so patients are intoxicated and ketotic without an acidosis, unlike methanol and ethylene glycol. Fomepizole is not indicated; supportive care is usual, with dialysis only for severe hemodynamic compromise.

CLOPIDOGREL.clue: P2Y12 inhibitor added to aspirin after coronary stenting and in selected acute coronary syndromes
CLOPIDOGREL.rationale: Clopidogrel blocks the platelet P2Y12 receptor. It is used with aspirin after stent placement and in many acute coronary syndromes; it is a prodrug and is held before major surgery when possible.

TERBINAFINE.clue: Oral antifungal used for nail dermatophyte infection; check the liver
TERBINAFINE.rationale: Oral terbinafine is first-line for many cases of onychomycosis and is also used for some scalp dermatophyte infections. Hepatotoxicity is the monitoring issue; it is not the treatment for yeast bloodstream infection.
